description: Blue-white pebbles, a good dozen, that will not melt in the palm. Whatever a Frostling is packed from, this is it.
lore: They are sold by the dozen because the game takes twelve. Every era that arrives here brought its own version — knucklebones, jacks, five-stones — and rime pebbles are what the game settled on in the cold country, being the one counter that will not warm, wear, or roll off true.

There is a patch on the north side of the meadow with eleven of them still in the grass, in a rough ring, where a throw was interrupted a long time ago. [[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]] cuts around it. Asked why she does not just gather them up, she says she will. The twelfth is in her apron pocket and has been for nine years.
gm_notes: Whose throw it was is not written and should not be. Solveig keeping the twelfth is the record; anyone who works out why has already understood her.
